job.title: Civil Works Manager
job.description:
Civil Works Manager

North Burnett Regional Council | Mundubbera, QLD | Civil Works & Infrastructure | Base salary up to $200K + housing support + vehicle allowance
  
North Burnett Regional Council is seeking a Civil Works Manager to lead its civil works and open spaces functions across the region. With a base salary of up to $200,000, this is an opportunity for an experienced infrastructure leader to shape service delivery, develop people and make a visible difference across six townships.
  
This position suits a pro-active leader who will get out across the region, spend time with their teams, understand the condition of the network, visit works in progress and actively resolve the issues that impact employees and the community.
  
With teams operating across six townships, visibility matters. The successful candidate will be expected to build strong relationships with staff, provide clear direction and create an environment where people feel supported, developed and accountable.
  
The Role
  
Reporting to the General Manager Works, you will lead the delivery of Council's civil works services across a diverse regional portfolio encompassing rural and urban roads, bridges, parks and open spaces, aerodromes and cemeteries.
The immediate priorities include strengthening delivery across the road network and supporting the people who deliver it.
  
Council is rebuilding momentum across its civil works program, with a strong focus on road renewals, resheeting, resealing and bridge repairs. You'll inherit capable people within the team, while having the opportunity to strengthen leadership, develop emerging talent and improve how works are planned, prioritised and delivered.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  
  • Providing visible, hands-on leadership across geographically dispersed civil works and open spaces teams
  • Leading, coaching and developing staff while building accountability, capability and succession
  • Overseeing the delivery and maintenance of Council's rural and urban road networks and associated infrastructure
  • Developing maintenance programs and identifying renewal priorities through sound asset management practices
  • Leading the planning and delivery of Council's civil capital works program
  • Managing operational and capital budgets and ensuring resources are directed to the areas of greatest need
  • Driving improvements in productivity, plant utilisation, safety and service delivery
  • Working closely with contractors, consultants and internal teams to achieve value-for-money outcomes
  • Building trusted relationships with stakeholders and communities across the North Burnett region
  • Providing clear, consistent and evidence-based advice while following issues through to resolution.
  
The formal position description reinforces this emphasis on visible leadership, staff capability, accountability and safety alongside asset management and capital delivery.
  
About You
  
You are an experienced civil works or infrastructure professional, but importantly, you are a leader who enjoys being involved.
  
You'll be comfortable walking into a depot and talking with frontline employees, visiting a road or project to understand an issue firsthand, mentoring an engineer who wants to progress their career, and then presenting clear and credible advice to senior leadership or elected members.
  
You will bring:
  • Strong experience across civil works, roads, infrastructure maintenance or construction
  • Proven experience leading operational and geographically dispersed teams
  • A hands-on and highly visible leadership style
  • A genuine commitment to coaching, mentoring and developing people
  • Strong asset management and capital works planning capability
  • Sound commercial, financial and project management experience
  • A practical understanding of safety within civil construction and maintenance environments
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to engage equally well with frontline staff, technical professionals, executives and elected members
  • Energy, initiative and a willingness to challenge existing ways of working and implement improvements
  • High levels of integrity, accountability and follow-through.
  
Council is open-minded regarding where you have developed your experience. You may already be working within local or state government, or you may come from civil construction, consulting or another infrastructure environment and be looking to bring your experience into a broader community-focused leadership role. The client specifically confirmed that local government experience is not essential and is interested in candidates who bring energy, ideas and the ability to implement change.
  
A Civil Engineering background and RPEQ would be highly regarded although this is not essential. More important is having the technical credibility to be an informed client and provide sound leadership across the function.
  
Why Join North Burnett Regional Council?
  
This is a role where you can see the impact of your leadership.
  
You'll have the opportunity to strengthen an established team, develop future leaders, rebuild momentum across the road network and introduce new ideas that improve how Council delivers services to its communities. Council sees a genuine opportunity for innovation and more cost-effective delivery as it continues a multi-year program of rebuilding its road network.
  
The package includes:
  • Base salary up to $200,000, depending on experience
  • $25,000 vehicle allowance
  • Remote locality allowance
  • $5,000 professional development allowance
  • Five weeks annual leave plus leave loading
  • Relocation assistance for the successful candidate
  • Access to Council housing in Mundubbera
  
If you're a civil infrastructure professional who believes leadership means being present, developing your people, communicating clearly and taking ownership of outcomes, this is an opportunity to have a genuine impact across an entire region.

job.title: Municipal Building Surveyor | Hobsons Bay City Council
job.description:
About Hobsons Bay City Council

Hobsons Bay City Council serves a diverse and established municipality in Melbourne’s inner west, encompassing residential neighbourhoods, established activity centres, industrial precincts and a range of community and Council assets.

Council’s building services function plays an important role in protecting community safety, responding to illegal building work and ensuring statutory obligations under the Building Act and Regulations are effectively delivered.

The service has recently undergone a realignment that has introduced clearer leadership across its two operational streams. A Deputy Municipal Building Surveyor now leads the building surveying function, while a Senior Building Surveyor oversees building site compliance and associated local laws activity.
This provides the incoming Municipal Building Surveyor with an experienced and stable team, a capable leadership structure and a strong platform from which to consolidate recent improvements and guide the future direction of the service.

Hobsons Bay is a values-led organisation committed to providing practical, responsive and community-focused services.

About the Role

The Municipal Building Surveyor is responsible for administering Council’s statutory building functions and providing leadership, technical oversight and strategic direction to an established team of approximately 11 staff.

The team operates across two complementary streams. The building surveying function includes the Deputy Municipal Building Surveyor, building surveyors, inspection, technical and administrative support. The building site compliance function is led by a Senior Building Surveyor and includes officers responsible for site safety and relevant local laws provisions.

The service undertakes a relatively small volume of municipal building permit work, with its primary focus sitting across enforcement, illegal building work, building safety and Council’s broader statutory responsibilities.

The incoming MBS will be supported by experienced practitioners who understand the municipality and service well. The team has good continuity, including several long-standing employees, and the recently appointed Deputy MBS provides capable day-to-day leadership across the building surveying function.

A recent review of the service identified a range of opportunities to strengthen processes, systems and operational practices. Many of these actions have already been progressed, with the new MBS responsible for ensuring improvements are fully embedded and that the service remains organised, responsive and transparent in reporting its workload, risks and priorities.
The role will also provide advice on emerging compliance matters, including swimming pool and spa safety obligations, while considering how Council can best support affected property owners and the wider community.

Over time, there is also scope to explore the future service model, including whether Council should broaden elements of its permit or inspection offering. Any future direction will need to be carefully considered against statutory responsibilities, organisational risk, insurance requirements and community benefit.

About You

You are an experienced building surveyor with Unlimited registration in Victoria and the technical capability required to perform the statutory responsibilities of a Municipal Building Surveyor.

You bring strong knowledge of building legislation, enforcement, compliance and regulatory decision-making, ideally developed across local government, private building surveying or a combination of both environments.
You are a practical and engaged leader who can provide clear technical direction while empowering an established Deputy MBS and senior practitioners to manage their respective areas effectively.

This is not a role requiring wholesale change. You will take the time to understand what is working, establish visibility over the team’s workload and priorities, and ensure recent improvements to systems and processes are sustained.

You are comfortable making considered statutory decisions, managing complex or sensitive enforcement matters and providing clear advice to senior leaders. You also bring the curiosity and commercial awareness to consider how the service could evolve while maintaining an appropriate focus on risk, community safety and Council’s legislative obligations.
Most importantly, you will bring energy, sound judgement and a collaborative leadership style to a team with strong technical knowledge and a genuine commitment to the Hobsons Bay community.
